chunks: He said: Abul Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Qummi, may Allah have mercy on him, reported to me, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, he said: Harun ibn Muslim narrated to me, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, peace be upon them both: "When you narrate a tradition to me, provide its chain of narrators for me." He said: "My father narrated to me, from my grandfather, from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, from Jibreel, peace be upon him, from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and everything I narrate to you is with this chain." And he said: "O Jabir, indeed a single tradition you receive from a truthful one is better for you than the world and all that is in it."

key_terms.إسناد: Chain of narration (isnad) — the linked sequence of transmitters verifying a hadith's authenticity
key_terms.حديث: Tradition (hadith) — a narrated saying, action, or tacit approval attributed to the Prophet or an Imam
key_terms.صادق: Truthful one (sadiq) — in this context, referring to the infallible Imam as the ultimate truthful source of knowledge

ai.seo_question: What chain of narration did Imam al-Baqir give to Jabir for all his teachings?
ai.summary: Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, a close companion of Imam al-Baqir (as), asked the Imam to provide chains of narration for his teachings. The Imam responded with the supreme chain of transmission: from his father, from his grandfather (Imam Husayn), from the Prophet, from Jibreel, from Allah Himself. He then emphasized that a single tradition from a truthful source surpasses the entire world in value, highlighting the Imam's direct connection to divine knowledge.
